title: Preparation of Tunable Extracellular Matrix Microenvironments to Evaluate Schwann Cell Phenotype Specification
protocol: Mix the PDMS base elastomer and curing agents using a pipette tip vigorously at a ratio between 10:1 and 60:1 until bubbles are homogeneously dispersed within the mixture.
Remove bubbles using vacuum desiccation until bubbles are dissipated.
Place a drop (~0.2 mL) of desiccated PDMS mixture on a square or circular coverslip (e.g., 22 mm x 22 mm).
Rotate the coverslip on a spin coater at 2500 rpm for 30 s.
Incubate the coverslip in either an oven at 60 °C for 1-2 h or room temperature overnight for PDMS to solidify.
Treat the coverslip using UV-Ozone cleaner for 7 min (UV wavelength: 185 nm and 254 nm) to increase the surface hydrophilicity.
Place it into a sterilized 6-well plate.
Immerse coverslips in the protein solution (10 µg/mL collagen I, fibronectin, or laminin) for 60 min in a sterile incubator at 37 °C.
Rotate the well plate to ensure each coverslip is covered with the protein solution.
Aspirate the protein solution and wash the coverslip with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) 3x.
Re-suspend RT4-D6P2T Schwann cell line from passaging dish using commercially available EDTA solution (1x) with 2.5% trypsin.
Count cells with hemocytometer.
Seed SCs on the tunable PDMS surface at the desired cell density.
Maintain cells in the desired cell culture parameters (90% humidity, 5% CO2, 37 °C) for the length of experiment.
Use Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% penicillin-streptomycin as the cell culture medium.
Draw the desired geometry and cell adhesive areas using computer-aided design (CAD) software.
Create a chrome photomask based on those patterns from a commercial supplier.
Use standard photolithography techniques in a clean room or dust-free environment.

Spin dispense photoresist SU-8 2010 on silicon wafers using a spin profile of 500 rpm for 10 seconds with an acceleration of 100 rpm/s followed by 3500 rpm for 30 seconds with an acceleration of 300 rpm/s.
Expose the wafer to UV light at an energy of 130 mJ/cm².
Bake silicon wafers at 190 °C for 30 minutes.
Place patterned silicon wafer inside a circular Petri dish, pour degassed PDMS (mixing ratio 10:1) onto the wafer.
Solidify PDMS on silicon wafer in an oven at 60 °C overnight.
Allow PDMS to cool to room temperature.
Cut stamps of 30 mm x 30 mm squares containing correct patterns from the silicon wafer using a surgical scalpel.
Sterilize PDMS stamps and tunable coverslips by immersing them into 70% ethanol for 30 min.
Dry the surface of PDMS stamps using a filtered air stream.
Pipette 50 µg/mL BSA (Texas Red conjugated) solution to cover the entire patterned side of the PDMS stamp.
Incubate PDMS stamps with BSA solution for 1 h at room temperature to allow for protein adsorption.
Dry the surface of tunable coverslips using a filtered air stream.
Increase surface hydrophilicity as described in step 1.1.5.
Air dry the PDMS stamps to remove the remaining BSA solution.
Bring the patterned side of the stamp into conformal contact with the tunable coverslip for BSA adsorption on the coverslip surface.
Gently press the stamp against the coverslip for 5 min.
Examine the micropattern using a fluorescence microscope with a FITC filter.
Substitute laminin for BSA protein to print cell adhesive areas instead of fluorescent patterns.
Repeat steps from 1.2.5 to 1.2.10 after substituting laminin for BSA.
Remove stamps from coverslips and transfer the coverslips into a sterilized 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL of 0.2% w/v Pluronic F-127 solution into each well, covering the surface of the coverslip.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Aspirate the Pluronic F-127 solution and wash 5 times with PBS.
Wash once more with cell culture medium before seeding cells.
Seed cells onto the coverslips at a density of 1,000 cells/cm².
After 45 minutes, remove the cell culture medium and wash the coverslips twice with PBS to prevent multiple SCs from adhering to the same pattern.
Maintain cells in the desired cell culture environment for 48 hours before quantification.
Prepare tunable PDMS surface coating two Petri dishes.
Perform microcontact printing to print line-patterned cell adhesive areas on one of the PDMS coated Petri dishes.
Fill the Petri dish with 4 mL of 0.2% w/v Pluronic F-127 solution and incubate for 1 h.
Rinse each side of the PDMS stamps with 70% ethanol 3x and dry with air.
Print unpatterned cell adhesive area using the unpatterned side of the stamp on the second Petri dish.
Aspirate F-127 solution from dishes, wash 3x with PBS followed by 1x wash using fresh cell culture medium.
Seed SCs on dishes at a density of 5,000 cells/cm² for line-patterned dishes and 10,000 cells/cm² for unpatterned dishes.
Maintain SCs at desired conditions for 48 h.
Transfer adequate RIPA buffer to a 10 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Dilute protease and phosphatase inhibitor at a ratio of 1:100 in RIPA buffer, mix well by pipetting.
Wash cells with ice cold PBS for 2 min.
Add 80 µL of the solution onto each cell adhesive area within petri dishes.
Incubate cells with the solution on an ice block for 15 min.
Scrape SCs with a cell scraper for 5 min.
Collect lysate into a labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Microcentrifuge lysate at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4°C.
Collect supernatant with a 1,000 µL pipette and transfer to a clean microcentrifuge tube.
Store cell lysate at -20 °C.
Pour the PDMS precursor into a 30 mm Petri dish.
Ensure the thickness of the PDMS layer is at least 20 mm in the Petri dish.
Remove the Petri dish with solidified PDMS from a 60 °C oven after 1 hour and allow to cool at room temperature.
Cut the polymer into 10 mm x 10 mm squares.
Measure the thickness of PDMS using calipers.
Place the PDMS on the stage of the compression force measuring machine.
Plug in the compression force sensor (model: 112C) to the sensor port and fix it to the axis of the test machine.
Adjust the height of the sensor to approximately 0.5 cm above the PDMS stamp using “jog” control on the front panel of the instrument.
Open the associated software using the “Test Setup” window, select “Servo profile”, and open the “Segment” window.
In the “Segment” window, input the desired “Control Rate” and “End Amount” for the test.
Use the “Z” button located on the control panel to reset all measurements at this point.
Move the sensor down to lightly contact PDMS until 1-2 newtons (N) are loaded.
Run the measurement using “Play” after utilizing the “Z” button, and save the file recording force and distance.
Seed SCs on substrates prepared from step 1.1.9 at a density of 5,000 cells/cm² in a 6-well plate.
Incubate SCs for 48 h in standard cell culture conditions (37 °C and 5% CO₂).
Dilute 12 μL of 10 mM Bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) stock solution into 12 mL of 37 °C cell culture medium to make a 10 µM BrdU labeling solution.
Remove the cell culture medium and wash SCs twice with PBS.
Add 2 mL of BrdU labeling solution into each well and incubate SCs for 2 h.
Remove BrdU labeling solution and wash SCs three times with PBS.
Add 1 mL of 3.7% formaldehyde in PBS to each well and incubate at room temperature for 15 min for cell fixation.
Wash substrate wells 3 times with PBS for 3 minutes each, ensuring the PDMS surface does not dry completely.
Aspirate formaldehyde solution and wash cells 3 times with PBS (3 min each).
Add 1 mL of 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS to each well to permeabilize cell membranes.
Incubate cells with Triton X-100 for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Remove Triton X-100 and wash cells 3 times with PBS (3 min each).
Add 1 mL of 1 N HCl into each well and incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Remove 1 N HCl, add 1 mL of 2 N HCl into each well, and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Remove 2 N HCl, mix 182 mL of 0.2 mM Na₂HPO₄ with 18 mL of 0.1 mM citric acid to produce a phosphate/citric acid buffer.
Add 1 mL of phosphate/citric acid buffer into each well and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Wash cells 3 times with 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS.
Add 2 mL of 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS to each well and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature to block nonspecific binding sites.
Dilute BrdU primary antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor 488 in a 3% BSA solution at a ratio of 1:300.
Incubate stem cells (SCs) with the staining solution overnight at room temperature while covered in aluminum foil.
Image SCs using the FITC and DAPI channels of a fluorescent microscope to detect BrdU and nuclei, respectively.
Save images as "nd.2" files.
Open “nd.2” files for each image taken at identical spatial positions.
Right-click on the background to open the window “Automated Measurement Results” and “Automated Measurement” in the section of “Analysis Control”.
Select “Count” from the “Count & Taxonomy” menu.
Click on each nucleus showing green fluorescence (BrdU positive) on FITC image and right-click on the image.
Repeat step to count the number of total nuclei for DAPI images.
Calculate the percentage of BrdU positive cells for this image.
Repeat steps 2.1.13 through 2.1.16 for other images for statistical purposes.
Calculate the mean percentage of BrdU positive cells for each substrate condition.
Apply camera settings identically across all samples with the same parameters.
Save images as “.nd2” files.
Open the image analysis software.
Right click background to open the window “Automated Measurement Results” and “Automated Measurement” in the section of “Analysis Control”.
Select “Object Data” in the “Automated Measurement Results” window.
Activate “Keep updating measurement” button.
Select “Measure” followed by “Object features” in the top panel of the software.
Add “Mean Intensity” to the section of “Selected for Measurement”.
Open and merge two “.nd2” image files that contain images of c-Jun and nuclei.
Select “ROI” and select “Draw Rectangular ROI” in the top panel.
Draw a rectangular area containing the nuclear area of a single cell.
Click “Full Image/Use ROI” to switch program from full image model to the ROI model in the new window after selecting “Define Threshold”.
Adjust the lookup table located on the left side of the window for adjustment of size/shape of the highlighted area within the rectangular ROI using “Intensity”.
Click the “OK” button.
Store data in the window of “Automated Measurement Results”.
Delete red highlighted area in the window of “Automated Measurement”.
Select a rectangular ROI using the “Pointing Tool” and delete it.
Repeat steps 2.2.6 to 2.2.11 for each additional cell.
Select “Stored” in the “Automated Measurement Results” window.
Export data to Excel.
Fix SCs prepared from step 1.2.22 following steps 2.1.5-2.1.7.
Perform nuclear staining using mounting medium with DAPI.
Acquire images of the sample using the DAPI channel and a 40x objective lens.
Save acquired images as “.nd2” files.
Open “Automated Measurement Results” window in the image analysis software.
Open “Automated Measurement” window in the image analysis software.
Select “Elongation” in the “Feature” column and add to “Selected for Measurements” column.
Activate “Keep Updating Measurement” function.
Open the “nd.2” image file containing nuclear images.
Select the “Auto Detect” function in the “Automated Measurement” window and choose a nucleus.
Right-click on the selected nucleus to display its aspect ratio in the “Automated Measurement Results” window.
Repeat steps 3.1 to 3.3 for quantifying nuclear aspect ratios of other nuclei within the image.
Select “Store Data” from the “Automated Measurement Results” window.
Repeat steps 3.1 to 3.4 for additional images.
Export the stored data to a spreadsheet file as previously done in section 2.2.13.
Follow standard protocols for performing western blot analysis detailed elsewhere.
Dilute rabbit anti-c-Jun antibody at 1:2,000.
Dilute mouse anti-β-actin antibody at 1:1,000.
Dilute rabbit anti-p75NTR antibody at 1:1,000.
Dilute rabbit anti-myelin basic protein antibody at 1:1,000.
Dilute anti-mouse/rabbit IgG HRP-linked antibody at 1:10,000.
